headline: Cornell's faculty voted no confidence in its leaders.
summary: Cornell's Faculty Senate voted 75-50 on Friday that it has no confidence in the administration's ability to address sexual assault on campus. A former student is suing the university and seven former fraternity members, saying she was raped at a fraternity house in 2024. The vote is symbolic. The board of trustees backs the president.
cover_answer: No. The vote is symbolic, and the trustees back him.
table_question: Should a leader lose the job for how they handled a problem?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: At a big college in New York, the teachers voted to say they don't trust the people in charge to keep students safe. It's like a whole class putting their hands up to say the rules aren't working. Someone was hurt, and the grown-ups are arguing about how it was handled. You are safe, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Hands up in class is the whole mechanism, and the hurt stays unnamed. This age reads your face first, so say it plainly.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, so the script gives them the vote and keeps the assault out: a class with its hands up saying the rules aren't working. Cantor says this age fears what it can picture, so nothing is pictured. Expect "who got hurt?" A grown-up student, and the grown-ups are dealing with it.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: A former Cornell student says she was raped at a fraternity party in 2024 and the school didn't take it seriously. It punished some of the men. Friday the professors voted 75-50 that they don't trust the leaders to fix it. Like a class voting on the principal: a message, but the trustees decide.
8-12.why: Report, punishment, vote, trustees: a chain, and a referee at the end.
8-12.why_long: At this age they are working out rules and whether adults apply them, so the script hands over the chain: a report, a punishment, professors who wanted more, a vote, and a board that decides anyway. Expect "so the vote did nothing?" The trustees' chair said it reflects deep anger on campus. Then she backed the president.

13-17.script: Should the people who run a place lose their jobs over how they handled something they didn't do? Cornell's professors voted 75-50 that they don't trust the leaders on sexual assault, after a former student sued saying she was raped at a fraternity. Second: 75-50 is a majority. Is it a mandate?
13-17.why: Two true things: 75 said the leaders failed, 50 said wait or no.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: 75 faculty said the leaders failed, and 50 voted no, some to wait for an outside review. The script asks what a no-confidence vote is for when it removes no one. Expect "were the men punished?" Two expelled, two suspended, two wrote papers; all seven deny it. The state is investigating.

5-7.q: Why don't they trust the grown-ups?
5-7.a: Someone was hurt, and the teachers think the people in charge didn't do enough to help. They voted to say so.

8-12.a: No. The trustees choose the president, and their chair backs him.

8-12.q: Why are they so angry at the school?
8-12.a: Some professors say he didn't act forcefully enough. He asked for more time.

13-17.q: Why vote if it can't remove anyone?
13-17.a: Pressure on the trustees. Their chair spoke of deep anger, and backed him.
Two expelled, two suspended, two wrote papers. All seven deny it.
